channel.title: Nature Materials
channel.description: Nature Materials is a multidisciplinary journal aimed at bringing together cutting-edge research across the entire spectrum of materials science and technology. Nature Materials covers all applied and fundamental aspects of the synthesis/processing, structure/composition, properties and performance of materials. Nature Materials provides a forum for the development of a common identity among materials scientists while encouraging researchers to cross established subdisciplinary lines. To achieve this, Nature Materials takes an interdisciplinary, integrated and balanced approach to all areas of materials research while fostering the exchange of ideas between scientists involved in different communities.

item.title: [7] Electron–phonon coupling and symmetry breaking in superconducting oxide interfaces near ferroelectric quantum criticality
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Jaume Gazquez, Wu Zhou

Authors: Roger Guzman, Miguel Pruneda, Jean Paul Nery, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Unconventional superconductivity, electron-phonon coupling, strongly correlated oxides, quantum criticality.

Tags: #unconventionalsuperconductivity #oxideinterface #electron-phononcoupling #quantumcriticality

Abstract: Nature Materials, Published online: 30 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02647-x Conductivity and superconductivity at the LaAlO3/SrTiO3 interface are well established. Now, in a layer-by-layer fashion, oxygen octahedra rotations, polar displacements and vibrational modes that are parallel and perpendicular to the interface are probed. A doping-dependent study reveals phonon modes related to oxygen vibrations, and their connection to superconductivity is discussed.

item.title: [7] A highly conductive polar metal with efficient charge–spin conversion
item.content:encoded:
Authors: Authors not available in source RSS

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Polar metal with efficient charge-spin conversion, relevant to spintronics and novel electronic properties.

Tags: #polarmetal #charge-spinconversion #inversionsymmetrybreaking #spintronics

Abstract: Nature Materials, Published online: 25 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02639-x The energy efficiency of spin-source materials can be increased by combining low resistivity and high charge–spin conversion in a single material. Now, a layered delafossite achieves this combination through polar distortions that break inversion symmetry while preserving high metallic conductivity.

item.title: [9] Giant and broadband circular dichroism from particle–hole symmetry breaking in Weyl semimetals
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Junhao Chu, Xiang Yuan

Authors: Xiangyu Jiang, Zeping Shi, Yuhan Du, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Giant circular dichroism in a magnetic Weyl semimetal, highly relevant to CD-ARPES and topological materials.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #Weylsemimetal #magnetictopologicalmaterial #circulardichroism #spectroscopy

Abstract: Nature Materials, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02630-6 The different Fermi velocities of particle and hole bands result in a giant mid-infrared circular dichroism in the magnetic Weyl semimetal Mn(Bi1−xSbx)2Te4.
